messages.author: 30e7367378ff5661
messages.subject: Spatial regression using INLA
parts:
Dear all,

I am currently using Integrated Nested Laplace Approximations (INLA) to model a spatio-temporal problem involving NO2 concentration data. Here are the specifics of my study:

  • I have mean daily NO2 concentration data spanning 5 years, collected from 18 different locations.
  • Alongside this, I have meteorological and traffic data for the same period.
  • I am modeling NO2 concentration over a 20x20 grid, which includes the 18 locations.
  • I use 15 locations for estimation and reserve 3 for validation.
  • For each day within these 5 years, I have 20x20 rasters of meteorological and traffic data within the grid.

Using INLA, I can successfully predict the spatial distribution of NO2 concentration on any specific date within the 5-year dataset. My question is:

Is it possible to predict NO2 concentration for a date outside the 5-year range, assuming we have the corresponding rasters of meteorological and traffic data for that unseen date?

Any insights or suggestions would be greatly appreciated.

Best regards

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Spatial regression using INLA
parts:
I think there is an example of your question in the SPDE book; see
https://www.r-inla.org/learnmore/books


btw, it might be more efficient to not use the SPDE approach to estimate the
parameters, you can use the model 'dmatern' for the 20 locations, and then,
depending on its use, use other means to get the predictions. at least, I would
check that out.


PS: if you're in for non-separable models, then check out
